Reigns developer Nerial enters 'hibernation mode,' lays off staff
The studio that gave birth to Reigns is ending operations—for now.
Bryant Francis
,
Senior Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
October 2, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
Image via Nerial/Devolver Digital
Nerial
, the celebrated British game studio behind the
Reigns
franchise,
Card Shark
, and
The Crush House
has announced it is entering 'hibernation mode,' ending development and laying off its remaining employees. The studio shared the news in
a post on social media
authored by co-founders François and Tamara Alliot, marking an end to its 13-year journey of making innovative and unusual games.
"Oh no, another one of those studio announcements with text on a somber background color?" it begins, in an allusion to the many posts that have accompanied
dozens of layoff announcements
that have hit the game industry since late 2022. "Unfortunately, yes, another one. Nerial is entering hibernation mode. After 13 years and 11 published games, we have decided together with our partners at Devolver to end development at the studio."
"It's been an incredible adventure," wrote the co-founders, saying they launched Nerial with "no expectations or ambitions." They urged other studios to hire the studio's "fabulous", crew of employees, heaping praise on each of them in a series of follow-up posts.
Related:
'Xbox is not for sale,' CEO Asha Sharma says
Additionally, they thanked the studio's many collaborators at Devolver Digital (which acquired the studio in 2021 and
laid off 40 percent of studio employees in 2024
) and other organizations that partnered with them on licensed titles like
Reigns: Game of Thrones
and
Reigns: The Witcher
.
François and Tamara said that it's "not the end of game dev" for them, but they need to take a break before "going back to their roots."
"We need to take a break and reflect on everything that's happened before coming back with a new perspective," they concluded.
Developers looking to commemorate the studio's legacy and learn more about the titles that gave it a distinct identity should be sure to read the developer-authored Deep Dives on the making of the complex systems powering
Reigns
and
The Crush House
.
